verdict.rationale: Bevy ships abundant examples and docs (bevy-docs-16, bevy-docs-17, bevy-docs-22, bevy-docs-33), which helps LLM familiarity, but the engine's API is explicitly non-stable — every release requires dedicated migration guides (bevy-docs-15) — and hands-on community reports confirm this instability breaks generated/existing code across versions ('had to make quite a few changes... this time it compiled out of the box!' bevy-comm-13) and caution against relying on it due to 'regular breaking changes' (bevy-comm-10). Docs are also called thin by users ('limited docs... out of resources when I get stuck', bevy-comm-14), undercutting the 'well-documented, stable APIs' premise LLMs need for first-try success. missing for 10: evidence of API stability across versions, LLM-specific benchmarks or first-try success reports, and resolution of the documented breaking-change/doc-thinness complaints.
